vocabulary.meaning: the complete disappearance of a species
examples: Habitat loss can push animals towards extinction.
Conservation aims to prevent extinction.
The species is officially classified as endangered.
Endangered animals need effective protection.

vocabulary.meaning: the variety of living species in an area or on Earth
examples: Biodiversity is declining in many regions.
Healthy ecosystems depend on biodiversity.

vocabulary.meaning: the destruction or reduction of the natural places where species live
examples: Deforestation causes major habitat loss.
Habitat loss is one of the biggest threats to wildlife.

vocabulary.meaning: the protection and careful management of nature
examples: Conservation programmes have helped some species recover.
International cooperation is important for conservation.

vocabulary.meaning: a group of living organisms that can reproduce with one another
examples: Scientists discover new species every year.
Some species adapt better to environmental change than others.

vocabulary.meaning: a community of living things and their environment
examples: The disappearance of one species can affect an entire ecosystem.
Pollution can damage fragile ecosystems.

vocabulary.meaning: the illegal hunting or capturing of wild animals
examples: Poaching threatens elephants and rhinos.
Park rangers work to prevent poaching.

vocabulary.meaning: a reduction in the number of individuals in a species or group
examples: The birds have suffered a rapid population decline.
Researchers are investigating the causes of the population decline.

vocabulary.meaning: to keep someone or something safe from harm
examples: Laws can protect endangered wildlife.
National parks protect important habitats.
